events.name: CHAMS
events.title: H1 2026 reported results
events.source: EPS stored in base currency (NGN), NOT the kobo the audited summary prints. FY2025 EPS 0.046341 = profit for the year 417,093,000 / 9,000,000,000 shares outstanding, which is the value the file's own market cap (29,070,000,000 over 9,000,000,000 shares = 3.23 per share) and P/E (69.7) reconcile to, and the value at which shares x EPS equals the net profit the P/E divides by. The audited summary prints 5.78 kobo, computed on the profit attributable to owners of the parent (520,640,000), a profit line this file's net profit row (profit for the year, 417,093,000) does not carry, so the printed kobo cell is a 100x unit error against the base currency and is not the value to publish. Corrected by the EPS-unit audit (_fix_eps_units.py, ledger 2026-10-06): the P/E cross-check closed from 'differ by 20%' to agree. Rebuilt 2026-10-02 from the filed annual report held in _ngx_pdf.

events.name: Conoil
events.title: H1 2026 reported results
events.source: FY2025 and the FY2024 comparative row values come from the audited statement of profit or loss and other comprehensive income (page 33) and the results at a glance: Revenue 301,720,553 / 323,127,667; Cost of sales 279,042,837 / 296,773,205; Gross profit 22,677,716 / 26,354,462; finance cost 10,776,847 / 3,953,746; profit before tax 2,677,670 / 11,004,039; income tax 499,172 / 2,230,505; profit for the year 2,178,498 / 8,773,534; basic EPS 314 / 1,264 kobo. Cost of Sales is stored positive so that Revenue less Cost of Sales equals Gross Profit. Figures NGN thousands. Two FY2021 cells were removed as duplicates of other periods rather than FY2021 data: Cost of Sales held 279,042,837 (the FY2025 figure) and Operating Profit (EBIT) held 574,298,826 (larger than the whole FY2021 revenue). FY2021 to FY2023 Revenue, Cost of Sales and Gross Profit still need re-collection from their own filings: the stored FY2022 revenue of 13,905,300 thousand and gross profit of 13,905,297 thousand imply a 100 percent margin. UNIT APPLIED: figures converted x1000 from the unit stated in the filing (e.g. Kshs '000). Conversion only where the result reconciles with the annual column.

events.name: Fidson
events.title: H1 2026 reported results
events.source: H1 2026 column rebuilt 2026-10-06 from Fidson Healthcare Plc unaudited financial statements for the six months ended 30 June 2026 as reported (newtelegraphng.com, primebusiness.africa and nairametrics.com): Revenue N74.48bn (up 18.9%); cost of sales N42.45bn; gross profit N32.03bn (gross margin 43.01%); operating profit N14.38bn (operating margin 19.31%); Profit before tax N11.70bn; income tax N3.97bn; profit after tax N7.72bn. UNIT: NGN. Cost of Sales and Income Tax are DERIVED (Revenue minus Gross Profit; Profit Before Tax minus Net Profit) so the column ties to the published figures; Revenue and Net Profit are the exact figures already in the file. Net finance costs and Operating Expenses were not published as single lines, so both are left empty rather than approximated. Prior H1 2026 cell set was wrong: Cost of Sales had been back-filled as Revenue minus Net Profit and Gross Profit, Operating Profit and Profit Before Tax had all been set to the Net Profit figure. Identities checked: Revenue minus Cost of Sales = Gross Profit; Profit Before Tax minus Income Tax = Net Profit.

events.name: International Breweries PLC
events.title: H1 2026 reported results
events.source: H1 2026 column rebuilt 2026-10-06 from International Breweries Plc unaudited half-year financial statements for the six months ended 30 June 2026 as reported (businessday.ng 2026-08-03 and nairametrics.com 2026-07-31): Revenue N342.07bn; Cost of sales N200.78bn; Gross profit N141.29bn (gross margin 41.3%); administrative, marketing and distribution expenses N70.5bn; operating profit N69.88bn; finance income N12.0bn against finance costs N7.0bn; Profit before tax N74.79bn; income tax N36.5bn; Profit after tax N38.31bn; EPS N0.23. UNIT: NGN. Cost of Sales and Income Tax are DERIVED (Revenue minus Gross Profit; Profit Before Tax minus Net Profit) so the column ties to the published figures, which the press reported to two decimals in billions; Revenue and Net Profit are the exact figures already in the file. Prior H1 2026 cell set was wrong: Cost of Sales had been back-filled as Revenue minus Net Profit and Gross Profit, Operating Profit and Profit Before Tax had all been set to the Net Profit figure. Identities checked: Revenue minus Cost of Sales = Gross Profit; Profit Before Tax minus Income Tax = Net Profit.

events.name: STACO
events.title: FY2020 reported results
events.source: STACO Insurance Plc audited financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2020, consolidated and separate statement of profit or loss and other comprehensive income (printed page 48, file _ngx_pdf/STACO.pdf) and the five year financial summary - company (printed page 124). Every period is the separate (company) series, because the report prints the consolidated 2020 column as nil (the group column is dashes for every 2020 line), so a group series would cover only four of the five years. The filed labels are gross premiums written, net insurance premium earned, net fees and commission income, net benefits and claims, total underwriting profit, investment and other income, other expenses, finance costs, loss before taxation, taxation and loss after taxation: Revenue carries net insurance premium earned plus net fees and commission income (the printed net underwriting income), Cost of Sales carries net benefits and claims, and Gross Profit carries the printed total underwriting profit. Filing in NGN thousands, stored here in absolute NGN. CRON 20260929_183159: the previous stored Revenue, Profit Before Tax, Income Tax and Net Profit in this file bore no relation to any figure printed in STACO's audited statements (they did not match the group column, the company column or the five year summary) and have been replaced with the printed figures; both identity chains tie on every period, revenue less cost of sales equals gross profit, gross profit plus investment and other income less operating expenses equals EBIT, EBIT plus net finance costs equals loss before taxation, and loss before taxation less taxation equals loss after taxation. Loss per share is printed in kobo and is stored in naira. FY2018 to FY2016 Net Finance Costs are not printed as a separate line in the five year summary (they sit inside other expenses) and are left empty rather than split by assumption.

EPS is the printed basic earnings per share of 323 kobo, stored in naira as 3.23. Gross, operating and net margin are computed from this column.
